chunks: And from him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Yazid al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"The woman who has been given the choice (in khula' or talaq al-khayr) does not inherit anything from her husband during her waiting period, because the bond of marriage has been severed between her and her husband from that moment, so there is no return (raj'ah) for him upon her, and there is no inheritance between them."

key_terms.الرَّجْعَة: The husband's right to take back his wife during the waiting period without a new contract
key_terms.الْعِدَّة: The waiting period for a woman after divorce or death
key_terms.الْعِصْمَة: The bond of marriage or contractual tie
key_terms.الْمُخَيَّرَةُ: The woman who has been given the choice to confirm or revoke the divorce

ai.seo_question: Does a woman who chooses divorce inherit from her husband during the waiting period?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the exercise of *khayr* (choice) by the wife in a *khul'* or conditional divorce scenario results in an immediate severance of the marital bond (*'ismah*), thereby nullifying the husband's right of *raj'ah* (retraction) and inheritance rights during the *'iddah*. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the specific mechanism of choice acts as a definitive termination of the contract, distinct from standard revocable divorces, ensuring legal clarity for the waiting period.
